answer.question: A handler finds a restricted item in a checked bag. What must happen to the bag, who approves the item, and how must the incident be reported?
answer.answer: The bag must be isolated and secured to prevent unauthorized access [1], and the restricted item must be removed from the baggage and secured for further review [2]. The Security Duty Manager must approve the item [3]. The incident must be reported under AP-INC-002, including details of the item, the baggage, and the location of discovery [2].

citations.document_title: AP-BAG-001 v2 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation
citations.excerpt: If a restricted item is found in a bag during baggage handling, the bag must not be handled further until it is approved or removed under the restricted-items approval procedure in AP-SEC-003. The baggage handler must notify the Baggage Duty Supervisor upon discovery of the restricted item. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for initiating the approval process or coordinating the removal of the restricted item. All bags containing restricted items must be isolated and secured to prevent unauthorized access. The handling of such bags must be conducted in accordance with security procedures. This ensures that restricted items are managed in compliance with applicable regulations and airport security policies.

citations.document_title: AP-SEC-003 v1 Staff Access, Restricted Items, and Approvals
citations.excerpt: A restricted item found in a checked bag must be handled in accordance with AP-BAG-001. The item must be removed from the baggage and secured for further review. The incident must be reported under AP-INC-002, including details of the item, the baggage, and the location of discovery. All relevant staff must follow the procedures outlined in these policies to ensure proper handling and documentation. The Security Duty Manager is responsible for coordinating the response and ensuring compliance with applicable regulations. The baggage must be isolated and inspected by security personnel before being returned to the owner or disposed of according to established procedures.

citations.document_title: AP-SEC-003 v1 Staff Access, Restricted Items, and Approvals
citations.excerpt: Approval to carry a restricted item airside must be granted in writing by the Security Duty Manager before the item passes the staff screening point. A Requesting Staff Member must submit a written request detailing the item, its purpose, and the intended location of use. The Line Manager must endorse the request to confirm its necessity and compliance with safety standards. The Security Duty Manager reviews and approves the request based on risk assessment and operational requirements. All approvals must be documented and retained for audit purposes. The request must include a justification for the item's necessity and a plan for its safe storage and disposal.

evidence.document_title: AP-BAG-001 v2 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation
evidence.text: When a baggage handler finds a damaged, leaking, or unattended checked bag in the baggage make-up area, the handler must escalate the incident to the Baggage Duty Supervisor within 10 minutes of discovery and must report it under AP-INC-002. All baggage incidents must be documented and reported to ensure proper follow-up. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for assessing the incident and determining the appropriate action. If necessary, the incident may be escalated to the ramp lead for further review. All staff must ensure that incidents are reported accurately and in a timely manner. This procedure ensures that all baggage issues are addressed in accordance with established protocols.
